newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher, Weyerhaeuser rumored to consider deal.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher, Weyerhaeuser rumored to consider deal.

text.p: Analysts speculated Monday that forestry companies Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd. and Weyerhaeuser Co. may consider an asset swap after Fletcher announced it was considering strategic alternatives for its Blandin operation in the United States.

According to market rumors, Fletcher might take Weyerhaeuser's North Pacific Paper Corp (NORPAC) newsprint subsidiary in Longview, Washington and Blandin, a maker of lightweight coated paper in Minnesota, could go to Weyerhaeuser.

"I've heard they are considering a trade with Weyerhaeuser where they would trade Blandin for NORPAC," said one analyst who declined to be identified. "It makes sense. It would help sharpen their focus."
TD Securities analyst Mark Kennedy also said the asset swap with Weyerhaeuser was a leading potential scenario although other companies might be interested in Blandin too.

Analysts did not have enough information to assess the potential terms of a deal, but they said it was likely Fletcher would also have to pay some cash for North Pacific because the operation is bigger.
Fletcher spokesman Jay Whitwham declined to comment on the Weyerhaeuser rumors.
But, he added that "any opportunities that come up that present the possibility of rationalizing product lines, we're certainly willing to take a look at them."
A spokesman for Weyerhaeuser, the biggest private owner of timberlands in the United States, declined comment.

Fletcher announced earlier it had retained Morgan Stanley to advise it on strategic options for Blandin, whose market is in the U.S. Midwest and is separate from the West Coast focus of Fletcher's other mills.
Whitwham said the investment bank would be contacting other forestry companies to guage their interest in Blandin and hoped to complete a review of options in two to three months.

Majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd, Fletcher has repeatedly said it wants to expand its newprint and specialty paper business, concentrating on the West Coast of North America and northern Pacific Rim.

Whitwham said Fletcher was "very keen" to grow its West Coast operations and would consider acquisitions. Fletcher has also been rumored to be interested in buying paper operations from MacMillan Bloedel Ltd.
Fletcher recently reaped C$588 million from the sale of its stake in lumber producer TimberWest Forest Ltd and refinancing of TimberWest's debt owed to Fletcher.
Blandin supplies magazine and catalog publishers and has capacity to make 475,000 tons of paper a year. An expansion will increase its capacity by 42,000 tons in 1998.
"They are looking to realign their paper asset base. Blandin wasn't a perfect fit for them," said TD Securities' Kennedy. He estimated Blandin's value at C$600 million to C$800 million.
For Weyerhaeuser, Blandin could offer an attractive outlet for its pulp production. "Weyerhaeuser is looking for ways to integrate more of their pulp production," Kennedy said.

North Pacific is 20 percent owned by Japan's Nippon Paper International and sells half its product to Japan. It has capacity for 700,000 tonnes of newsprint a year, making it one of the biggest newsprint mills in North America.
As Weyerhaeuser's only newsprint operation, "it would seem somewhat of an orphan for them" and a potential candidate for divestiture, said one analyst who declined to be identified.
